towerFacts.plan_notes: Rectangular (not square). OSM footprints: North Bldg (200 Locust) 32.9 x 21.4 m, South Bldg (220) 32.2 x 22.7 m, West Bldg (210) 34.1 x 22.8 m — model as ~33 x 22 m. This equals an 18-bay x 12-bay grid on a 6 ft (1.83 m) planning module (18 x 1.83 = 32.9 m; 12 x 1.83 = 22.0 m), consistent with SAH's note that the exposed structural grid modules are 'keyed to interior room dimensions'. Cast-in-place load-bearing concrete perimeter (facade IS the structure) + interior core; originally 8 apartments per floor, ~240 units/tower, studios to 3BR. Three identical towers in a pinwheel arrangement around the plaza (tower centroids: N 39.94582,-75.14468; W 39.94555,-75.14512; S 39.94504,-75.14454).

facade.window_pattern: Uniform egg-crate grid, identical on all 4 faces, all 31 floors. Bay pitch ~1.83 m (6 ft). Photogrammetry from high-res photos (Wikimedia PA1, Canon EOS 6D): per bay, bright mullion face ~11 px vs window opening ~37 px of a 48 px pitch, i.e. mullion face ~0.42 m wide, window opening ~1.40 m wide. VERTICAL window proportions — openings are TALLER than wide (~1.4 m w x ~2.2 m h, ratio ~1:1.55), floor-to-ceiling glass. Vertical rhythm per ~2.9 m floor: glass ~2.2 m + concrete spandrel zone ~0.7 m (spandrel face reads slightly thicker than mullion face, with strong horizontal shadow lines because the grid projects). Glass recessed deep behind the grid face — estimated 0.35-0.5 m reveal (published descriptions: aluminum-framed floor-to-ceiling windows 'set deep into the concrete screen'; 'deeply recessed windows that cast crisp shadows'). Grid members have slightly eased/chamfered inner edges; each cell reads as a picture-frame around dark glass.
facade.corner_treatment: Solid concrete corner piers: the corner member is visibly wider than field mullions (~1.5-2x, est. 0.6-0.9 m of solid concrete on each face), forming an L that turns the corner; no corner windows, crisp square arris.
facade.ground_floor: Tower grid terminates on a plain flat soffit/edge band above a tall recessed glass lobby storey (~1.5-2x a typical floor, est. 5-6 m). Slender square concrete columns at the ground carry the grid at wider spacing — approximately every 3rd grid line (~5.5 m o.c., so ~7 columns on the long face, ~5 on the short face), creating an open colonnade with the dark-glass lobby wall set well back (several meters). Verified from 2018 Google photosphere at the plaza.
facade.roof: Flat roof. Facade caps with a plain, slightly deeper concrete fascia/parapet band (no cornice). Low mechanical penthouse set back from all edges: a long 1-story slab-like strip (roughly half to two-thirds of the roof's long dimension), same buff concrete color; thin antenna masts on some towers.
facade.balconies: NONE - confirmed from all photos; facades are perfectly flat grids on all four sides.

site.plaza: Brick-paved plaza/forecourt between the three towers with a circular vehicular drop-off drive (brick/cobble paving, granite curbs); flagpoles; mature trees and landscaped lawn berms around the 4.8-acre tower parcel; towers sit slightly above surrounding streets (grass slopes up from 2nd St). Main vehicle entry off 2nd Street with small guard booth.
site.sculpture: Leonard Baskin 'Old Man, Young Man, The Future' (1966, bronze, his first major outdoor work): standing Young Man 6'3", seated Old Man 6'5" on a cube, winged bird-creature 'The Future' 4'3" on a tall base; low brick base/platform ~10 ft wide. Located on the plaza at the circular drive beside the fountain, near the 2nd & Locust St entry (approx 39.94525,-75.14490, SE of the North tower).
site.townhouses: 37 three-story brick townhouses by Pei on 2.8 acres in five clusters arranged in quadrangle courtyard patterns, immediately west/southwest of the towers (3rd & Locust area); flat roofs, ~10 m tall (OSM height tags 9.75-11.27 m), individual footprints ~6.4 x 12.8 m (OSM), brick walls with arched entryways, private courtyards behind brick walls with iron gates.
site.parking: 350-space underground garage beneath the tower parcel (plus some surface parking); OSM marks the underground garage access at 39.94491,-75.14527 (west side, near the West tower); ramp reached from the internal circular drive. A small ~1,500 sq ft shopping/commercial pavilion also sits on the parcel.

towerFacts.confidence_notes: Published, high confidence: 31 stories; 94.2 m / 309 ft (CTBUH SkyscraperCenter for Towers I & III; OSM tags height=89 and levels=32 — the 32 likely counts the mechanical penthouse; some listings say 292 ft, but 309 ft is the CTBUH figure — for an 89 m vs 94 m discrepancy, prefer ~94 m to the roof parapet); cast-in-place load-bearing concrete grid facade with floor-to-ceiling aluminum-framed windows set deep in the concrete screen (SAH Archipedia snippet, PCF website); 624 (Wikipedia) / 614 (HOA) units, 8 units/floor; 37 townhouses (PCF); 350 underground spaces (HOA); Baskin sculpture dimensions (Association for Public Art). Footprints 32-34 x 21-23 m are OSM-traced (±1-2 m). ESTIMATED from photo measurement (stated as such): bay counts 18 x 12 (pixel-pitch analysis of Wikimedia PA1 gave 18.2 bays on the long face at ~48 px pitch; visual count of the short face in the closeup photo gave ~12; these also exactly reconcile the OSM footprint with a 6-ft module, but no drawing was found confirming 18/12 — treat as high-probability estimate); mullion ~0.42 m vs window ~1.40 m (11:37 px duty cycle, +/-10%); glass height ~2.2 m and spandrel zone ~0.7 m (noisier vertical profile); recess depth 0.35-0.5 m (visual estimate from oblique photos only); ground-floor colonnade spacing 'every 3rd grid line' and lobby height 5-6 m (read from a 2018 Google photosphere, low resolution); corner pier width (visual). Floor-to-floor 2.92 m is derived (94.2 m minus tall lobby and parapet over 30 residential floors), not published. Colors sampled from photos: sunlit concrete #E9E5D4, neutral/shade ~#C8C3B2 (warm buff exposed-aggregate); glass reads dark blue-gray #37343F (clear glass, dark interiors, dark anodized frames).

landmarks.name: Saint Peter's Church
landmarks.note: Georgian red-brick nave (1761) with Strickland's 1842 six-stage brick tower and slender white wooden octagonal spire, 210 ft total - the tallest thing in Society Hill's low skyline

landmarks.name: Old Pine Street Church
landmarks.note: Greek Revival 1857 remodel: cream/tan stuccoed temple front with giant Corinthian colonnade and low-pitched pediment, no tower or spire

landmarks.name: Mother Bethel African Methodist Episcopal Church
landmarks.note: Muscular 1890 Romanesque Revival in rough-faced white granite (weathered gray), asymmetric four-story corner bell tower with pyramidal cap and big arched openings (tower height estimated from photos)

landmarks.name: Merchants' Exchange Building
landmarks.note: Strickland 1834 Greek Revival in pale Pennsylvania marble; semicircular Corinthian portico on the Dock St end crowned by a 40-ft Lysicrates-monument lantern tower (total height estimated from 3-story block + 40-ft lantern)

landmarks.name: Head House
landmarks.note: Small 1804 two-story red-brick firehouse with white wooden cupola and weathervane; the one-story open brick arcade market shed (the Shambles, ~5 m tall) runs a full block south down the middle of 2nd St

landmarks.name: Society Hill Synagogue
landmarks.note: Thomas U. Walter 1829/1851 classical-Italianate former Baptist church; pale painted-stucco facade with paired entrance doors and parapet, no tower (heights estimated)

landmarks.name: Old Saint Mary's Church
landmarks.note: 1763 red-brick Catholic church with plain gable and Gothic-arched window detailing from an 1880s refacing; no tower, churchyard in front (heights estimated)

landmarks.name: Old Saint Paul's Church
landmarks.note: 1761 red-brick Episcopal church, simple pedimented gable front with arched windows, no tower or spire; set back behind iron fence (heights estimated)

landmarks.name: Hopkinson House
landmarks.note: Stonorov 1962 modernist slab on Washington Square, 91.8 m / 35 CTBUH floors (marketed as 33 stories): buff-tan brick panels in an exposed concrete grid with stepladder pattern of protruding balconies, flat roof with mechanical penthouse

landmarks.name: The Residences at Dockside
landmarks.note: 17-story 1995 condo slab sitting on a pier in the Delaware; light gray precast facade with long horizontal white balcony rails and a stepped, rounded crown (height estimated from 17 stories)

landmarks.name: One Independence Place
landmarks.note: 75.3 m / 25-story 1980s dark red-brown brick condo tower (twin of 2 Independence Place), square plan with chamfered/notched corners of stacked balconies, flat roof

landmarks.name: 2 Independence Place
landmarks.note: 74.7 m / 25-story near-identical twin just north of One Independence Place; same dark red-brown brick with corner balcony notches, flat roof

landmarks.name: City Tavern
landmarks.note: 1975 faithful reconstruction of the 1773 Georgian tavern: 3.5-story red brick with white trim, dormered hipped-gable roof and tall chimneys to ~15 m (heights estimated)

landmarks.name: Athenaeum of Philadelphia
landmarks.note: John Notman 1847 Italianate palazzo, one of America's first brownstone facades: chocolate-brown sandstone, 3 stories, bracketed cornice, flat roof (height estimated)

landmarks.name: Hill-Physick House
landmarks.note: 1786 freestanding 4-story Federal brick mansion (rare for the rowhouse district), famous giant fanlight over the door, low hipped roof, walled garden (height estimated)

landmarks.name: Saint Stanislaus Church
landmarks.note: Mid-19th-c. brick former Protestant church bought by the Polish parish in 1890; gable-front red brick with arched windows and only a modest cross/finial above the gable, no tall spire (heights estimated from photos)

landmarks.name: Holy Trinity
landmarks.note: 1789 German Catholic church at 6th & Spruce: plain Georgian red-brick meeting-house form, gable set perpendicular to Spruce so the altar faces east, no tower (heights estimated)

landmarks.name: Kesher Israel Synagogue
landmarks.note: 1796 former Universalist church converted 1889; red-brick gable front with arched windows and an ornate 1896 Romanesque/Colonial Revival 'Pompeian' entrance surround, no tower (heights estimated)

landmarks.name: Old Pine Community Center
landmarks.note: Modest 3-story modern brick community building at 4th & Lombard, flat roof, unornamented (heights estimated)

landmarks.name: Penn's Landing Great Plaza
landmarks.note: Low fan-shaped concrete amphitheater terraces stepping down to the Delaware with a small stage canopy - essentially flat hardscape, ~5 m max (estimated; site slated for redevelopment)

landmarks.name: Independence Seaport Museum
landmarks.note: Long 2-story pavilion at Walnut St on the waterfront with a big curved gray metal roof and glazed frontage (height estimated)

landmarks.name: Sheraton Society Hill
landmarks.note: Low-slung 4-story 1986 red-brick hotel on Dock St's curving alignment, designed to defer to the historic district: pitched slate-gray roofs, courtyard plan (height estimated)
